sentences.text: After the accident, the deceased was taken to Government Hospital, Hosadurga, for first aid and then shifted to Sahyadri Narayana Hospital, Shimoga.
He was then shifted to Metro United Health Centre for 2 days, whereafter, he was admitted to Kasturba Hospital, Manipal on 13.05.2016 and treated up to 10.06.2016.
On union of fracture and vitals being normal
, he was discharged.
Meanwhile, claim petition was also filed seeking compensation for the injuries sustained.
5) Subsequently, on 10.04.2017, he was re-admitted to Wenlock District Hospital, Mangaluru.
The admission register notes that there was malunion of right tibia.
He remained hospitalized as in-patient and underwent further treatment till 02.08.2017, i.e., the date when he passed away.
The amended claim petition was filed and compensation for death was also claimed.

6) The post-mortem was conducted on 03.08.2017 and as per the report, the histopathological examination report stated as under  Histopathological Examination  Portion of the lung tissue showed pulmonary oedema with bronchopneumonia, portion of the blood clot from the pulmonary truck-postmortem clot.

7) To rule out the possibility of any other cause of death, the CA No. / 2025 (@SLP (C) No. 8642/
2022) histopathological examination was sent to Regional Forensic Science Laboratory for further opinion, which in its report dated 25.10.2017 and 24.11.2017 stated as under  Residues of Volatile poisons, Pesticides, Barbiturates, Benzodiazepine group of drugs, Toxic metal ions and anions were not detected in the above stated exhibits.
xx xx xx
xx Final opinion  Based on autopsy finding and Chemical Examiners report I am of the opinion that the deceased died due to complications secondary to bronchopneumonia.
However, the death due to consumption of poisonous substance is ruled out.

In sequel of the said factual context, the finding recorded by MACT, in particular para 31 and affirmed by High Court that the victims death has no nexus with the injuries sustained in the accident requires to be looked into.

8) The High Court in the impugned judgment opined that MACT erred in dismissing the claim petition in toto and partly allowed the appeal granting reimbursement for medical treatment plus other miscellaneous expenses incurred during treatment because of accident.
The High Court granted compensation under the following heads

Travelling expenses, accommodation charges,
Rs. 49,500/-
food and attendant charges [Rs. 1500/- per day for 33 days] Reimbursement of expenses incurred for Rs. 2,16,073/-
 medical treatment  CA No. / 2025 (@SLP (C) No. 8642/ 2022)
 Miscellaneous expenses Rs. 25,000/-
 Total after rounding off Rs. 2,91,000/- along with  interest at the rate of 9%

sentences.text:
In absence of grant of any compensation for death, the short question that falls for consideration is whether in the facts and circumstances, deceased, MR. G.V.
Manjunatha died due to injuries and complications developed due to accident caused on 08.05.2016?
If yes, what amount of compensation are the dependents of the deceased entitled to?
10) We have heard learned counsels for the parties at length and perused the material placed for consideration.
11) The factum of accident on 08.05.2016 is not in dispute.
Hospitalisation of deceased to various hospitals on account of injuries received as referred above is also not in dispute.

It is also not in dispute that because of those injuries, the deceased took first aid from Government Hospital,
Hosadurga, whereafter, he was admitted to Sahyadri Narayana Hospital, Shimoga, then at Metro United Health Center, followed by admission to Kasturba Hospital, Manipal and lastly at Wenlock District Hospital Mangalore, where he breathed his last.
The existence of insurance policy on the date of accident is also not in dispute.

Therefore, at this stage, CA No. / 2025 (@SLP (C) No. 8642/
2022) only the findings as recorded by MACT that there is no nexus of the accident and injuries sustained with the cause of death is required to be seen.
12) The High Court in the impugned judgment recorded that due to the accident, the deceased got admitted in the Hospital and incurred medical expenses for treatment.

To understand whether deceased died due to injuries sustained in the accident, it is relevant to refer the examination in chief of the Doctor Jagadish Rao (PW3), who conducted autopsy of the deceased.

He has categorically deposed that as per his final opinion on the post-mortem, the death is due to secondary infection of the injuries sustained by the deceased in RTA which leads to bronchopneumonia.

Further, he has clearly spelt out that the reason for death is due to the complications (sepsis)
secondary to bronchopneumonia (infection of lungs) which may be due to prolonged hospitalization and debulated conditions of the deceased due to injury sustained as a result of injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.

Additionally, in the cross-examination, the doctor in particular para 4 thereof, has specifically denied the suggestion put on behalf of the Insurance Company that there was no relation with the injuries and the death of the injured - G.V. Manjunatha.

13) Reverting to the post-mortem report, it is found that under the histopathological examination,
the doctor opined that the portion of the lung tissue showed pulmonary oedema with bronchopneumonia, portion of the blood clot from the pulmonary truck-postmortem clot; however,
under the CA No. / 2025 (@SLP (C) No. 8642/ 2022) head of Final Opinion, it was said that the cause of death shall be furnished after the perusal of Chemical Examiners report.

A bare perusal of Chemical Examiners report dated 25.10.2017 and 24.11.2017, makes it clear like daylight that the M Manjula vs The National Insurance Co. Ltd on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122218309/
3 death is caused due to complications secondary to bronchopneumonia and the allegation of poisonous substance has been ruled out.
14) In view of placing the said positive evidence on record and the statement of Doctor Jagdish Rao (PW 3), the defence as taken by the Insurance Company before MACT that cause of death may be due to consumption of some poisonous substance holds no ground and is liable to be repelled.

sentences.text:
15) During hearing, learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company has made an unsuccessful attempt to show that in June, 2017, when deceased was admitted in Sahyadri Narayana Hospital, Shimoga, the deceased sought discharge contrary to medical advice, and therefore,
complications, if any, developed, were because deceased did not adhere to the medical advice and had not taken proper treatment.

In our view, at this stage the said argument does not merit consideration and such plea cannot be allowed to be raised by the Insurance Company, once they have taken the defence that cause of death is because of corruption of poisonous substance.
It is not a case in which the deceased has not taken treatment and continuous treatment taken at various Hospitals belie such argument.
Therefore, said contention is not acceptable.

16) Having considered the above discussion, we can safely conclude that the finding as recorded by the MACT and affirmed by High Court that there is no nexus between death of deceased and the accident is without due appreciation of the material placed on record.

In view of the said conspectus,
we are of considered opinion that the High Court has also committed an error in granting compensation only to the extent under pecuniary heads and not for death while confirming the findings of MACT qua the same.
Therefore, the compensation in the case ought to be awarded on account of the accident and the injuries received due to which G.V. Manjunatha succumbed.

17) In the said context, if we calculate the amount of compensation looking to the date of accident,
that is, 08.05.2016: the deceased was an agriculturist and his earning can fairly be accepted Rs.
8,000/- per month.
On adding 40% towards future prospects, the same comes to Rs. 11,200/-.

As the number of dependents were 4 at the relevant time, therefore, 1/4 th towards personal expenses has to be deducted, whereafter, the loss of dependency per month comes to Rs. 8,400/- and annually it would be Rs. 1,00,800/-.
By applying the multiplier of 15, the total loss of dependency annually comes to Rs. 15,12,000/-.

If we add Rs. 75,000/- towards expenses for transportation of dead body and cremation charges Rs. 40,000/- for loss of consortium to the wife and loss of love and affection to the two children is Rs. 1,20,000/- and same is awarded.

18) In addition, from the date of accident till death, medical expenses CA No. / 2025 (@SLP (C) No.
8642/ 2022) incurred are Rs. 2,16,073/- on addition of which, the total amount of compensation comes to Rs. 19,63,073/- which we round off to Rs. 19,65,000/-.
This amount shall substitute the compensation awarded by the High Court.
19) In view of the foregoing, the present appeal filed by the appellants- claimants stands allowed in part setting aside the finding of MACT and modifying the Award of the High Court.

The amount of compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the filing of the claim M Manjula vs The National Insurance Co. Ltd on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122218309/
4 petition till its realization.
